                                        ten require frequent updates due to platform-specific APIs,
                                        visual agents leveraging Multimodal Large Language Mod-                                                                                 Position: [380, 540, 620, 460]

                                        rectly with Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs). However,
                                        these agents face significant challenges in visual percep-

into 336x336 or 448x448 grids, though this could impact
efficiency and contextual understanding across grid bound-        The core goal of Information-Sensitive Cropping (ISC) is
aries. More recent architectures like Qwen2-VL [35] intro-        to dynamically segment a high-resolution screen image into
duce dynamic resolution support through innovations such          smaller, variable-sized sub-images based on the distribu-
as 2D-RoPE and multimodal position embedding, allowing            tion of visual information. This adaptive approach ensures
flexible processing of varying image sizes while maintain-        that each sub-image captures a relatively balanced amount
ing positional information. Despite these methods’ ability        of meaningful information, avoiding the pitfalls of uniform
to handle high-resolution inputs, they share a common lim-        cropping strategies that can either neglect critical details or
itation of treating all pixels and regions equally, leading       waste computational resources on irrelevant regions. The
to significant efficiency issues when processing GUI im-          ISC process is structured into three key steps: information
ages where information is unevenly distributed. In contrast,      detection, adaptive cropping, and uniform resizing. Each
our approach dynamically adapts computational resources           step is described below.
based on information density, enabling more efficient pro-        Information Detection. We employ edge detection to iden-

SRDL successfully mines and learns from challenging
cases, achieving performance comparable to or better than
models trained with 10x more annotated data.

4.3. Evaluation on Agent Benchmarks
We assess Iris’s practical utility on two comprehensive
agent benchmarks: Mind2Web[11] for web interactions
and Android In the Wild (AITW)[29] for mobile OS tasks
(Tab. 3 and Tab. 4). We follow the same evaluation setting
as SeeClick [9]. The detail of the benchmarks and compar-
ison models are provided in Appendix Sec. 10.
   Across both benchmarks, Iris consistently outperforms
SeeClick by significant margins, achieving best perfor-

                                                                      5. Conclusion
                                                                      This paper introduces Iris, a foundational visual agent that
                                                                      advances GUI understanding through two key innovations:
                                                                      Information-Sensitive Cropping (ISC) and Self-Refining
                                                                      Dual Learning (SRDL). ISC enables efficient processing of
                                                                      high-resolution interfaces by adaptively allocating compu-
                                                                      tational resources based on information density, achieving a
                                                                      300% efficiency improvement over traditional approaches.
                                                                      Rather than treating all regions equally, ISC employs edge
                                                                      detection to identify visually dense areas and dynamically
                                                                      adjusts token allocation, allowing for detailed processing
                                                                      of complex UI elements while efficiently handling sparse
Figure 5. SRDL’s effectiveness across different case mining strate-
gies.                                                                 regions. SRDL enhances model robustness through au-
                                                                      tonomous discovery and learning from challenging cases,
SRDL Analysis: Both Visual and Functional Hard Case                   delivering a 10% accuracy gain without requiring additional
Mining are Essential. Our analysis of SRDL’s hard case                manual annotations. Evaluations on multiple benchmarks,
mining strategy reveals the critical role of both visual and          ranging from basic GUI grounding to complex multimodal
functional components. As shown in Fig. 5, the baseline               agent tasks, demonstrate that Iris achieves state-of-the-art
model without SRDL achieves 64.7% accuracy, while in-                 performance while balancing both accuracy and efficiency,
corporating SRDL with either visual or functional mining              setting a new standard for GUI-based digital agents.

We evaluate Iris on two comprehensive agent benchmarks
following the same settings as SeeClick [9]: AITW [29] for
mobile OS interactions and Mind2Web [11] for web navi-
gation.
